This mapping is defined by a set of constraints including readiness blockers B, approval boundary A, review sections S, command intents I, expected evidence E, and forbidden targets F. The operator enforces that P does not contain executable shell commands and never sets livePromotionAllowed=true. The approval boundary A is computed as a scalar threshold from R such that A = f(R), where f is a monotonic function ensuring readiness is sufficient for approval. Command intents I are validated against expected evidence E to ensure consistency. Forbidden targets F are filtered out of P to prevent unsafe operations. The system avoids live execution by design, making it a purely observational construct. Failure modes include invalid readiness input, inconsistent intent-evidence pairs, and violation of forbidden target constraints.
